brief: Goldman macro trader Faris Mourad argues index performance still depends on energy volatility and the 10-year yield allowing thematic rotations to run, evidenced by house baskets (AI pair +7.7%, HALO +6.0%, megacap-vs-unprofitable-tech +3.9%) rallying this week while the S&P was flat this month. He flags five trades. First, agentic AI reshaping consumer shopping is a 3-5+ year transition analogous to eCommerce; the Agentic-vs-Consumer-Inertia trade should keep working, and adoption should also lift cybersecurity/fraud-prevention demand. Second, short Non-Profitable Tech: the 10-year has risen for 7 straight months, tied for the longest streak in 50 years, and the basket is down 11.8% this month after outperforming the S&P by 20+ points over the past year. Third, buy Power as a catch-up trade after the DOE committed $5.25bn to grid projects adding 20+GW, benefiting Europe's power/renewables too. Fourth, Europe fiscal divergence: bullish German Fiscal Beneficiaries (debt/GDP under 65%), bearish French Domestics (debt/GDP to 125% by 2030, OAT-Bund +100bp) via December put spreads, though French Banks show near-term relief. Fifth, Brazil's pre-election trade: least-owned market, upside skewed to a Bolsonaro win via a rate basket that could re-rate 30%+ if 200-300bps of cuts get priced. None survives a 6% 10-year or another oil spike.
